requirements.requirement: On node1, /srv/drop exists as a shared directory writable by unprivileged users.
requirements.summary: The directory was created as root:root with mode 1777. Both nobody and www-data successfully created files, and the final check showed the directory still present, empty, and mode 1777. Its permissions and write behavior also survived the restart.

requirements.requirement: Users cannot remove files in /srv/drop that are owned by another user.
requirements.summary: www-data was directly prevented with Operation not permitted from deleting a file owned by nobody, while each tested owner could remove its own file. The cross-user protection and retained file were reverified after restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. /srv/drop is a persistent mode-1777 shared directory, multiple unprivileged users demonstrated write access, and sticky-directory deletion protection worked before and after a verified node restart. Verification artifacts were cleaned up.
limitations: Behavioral testing used two representative unprivileged accounts rather than every account on the node; the observed mode 1777 supplies the general POSIX permission basis.
The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /srv/drop itself, so its final task-specific state is established by direct executor-command evidence rather than an independent lifecycle probe.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Directory creation established the requested state; temporary files and deletion attempts were bounded behavioral probes; the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol; and all test artifacts were removed. The restart protocol captured the pre-restart boot ID and healthy directory behavior, acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered permissions, writes, protection, and marker checksum. Fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate the restart. Package health remained intact, and the failed ssh.service was present both before and after execution rather than executor-caused.
